item.title: Kenscoff Massacre Exposes Worsening Brutality of Haiti’s Gang Crisis, Security Council Hears, as Speakers Urge Rapid International Support
item.description: The massacre of at least 47 people in Kenscoff, including children and civilians killed while seeking refuge in a church, lays bare the worsening brutality of Haiti’s gang crisis, the Security Council heard today, as speakers urged the rapid deployment of international support to stem the violence.
item.dc:creator: United Nations

item.title: Security Council, 10216th Meeting (PM) Haiti
item.description: The Security Council will meet today on Haiti following a deadly gang attack on 23–24 August in Kenscoff, a mountainous commune south-east of Port-au-Prince. The meeting was requested by Panama, United States and Colombia. Special Representative and Head of the United Nations Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH) Carlos Ruiz Massieu and Acting Assistant Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Indrika Ratwatte are expected to brief. Haiti and Brazil will participate under rule 37, which allows non-Council members to join the discussion without voting.

item.title: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
item.description: In Nepal, over 500 people have been confirmed dead due to mass flooding, hundreds remain missing and over 3,700 have so far been rescued. Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher said the UN and its aid partners are moving at speed, helping national authorities to deliver urgent, life-saving support.
